W2 (empirical), after E039. Tip is E036: 5.314 s, 0.7532 on seeds 0-2. Fresh seeds 13-22 (E038) gave 0.7525; held-out means run 0.1-0.2 pp under seeds 0-2, so the population mean is about 0.752 and the 0.75 bar has about 0.2 pp of headroom.

Mechanisms, each tied to measured runs:
1. Epoch dial: about 5% of time per 0.5 epoch for 0.0-0.25 pp (E020, E023, E027). E034 stacked a freeze with +0.5 epoch and saved 0.40 s versus E027 at about 0 pp.
2. EMA (+0.97 pp, E005) and Muon (+0.66 pp, confounded, E006) are in the tip. About 8 time-neutral boosters failed (E025, E029, E030, E032, wd, LS and others). Averaging, LR shape and wd sit at a flat optimum within about ±0.2 pp. Anything that cuts training signal costs accuracy (E030, E032, E037, E039).
3. Time tracks pixels. Early low resolution is nearly free (E026, E033). The 28 and 32 px phases carry the accuracy (E018, E024).
4. Backward truncation on memory-bound large maps is the best lever (E028, E034, E036). E037 moved the freeze to 60%. It saved 0.25 s but cost 0.38 pp, about 0.65 s per pp, near break-even. E039 (BN folding) saved only about 0.03 s and lost 0.15 pp, so the stem is nearly exhausted.
5. Noise: identical code is bit-identical. Any change to step count or RNG use reshuffles the 3-seed mean by about ±0.2 pp. Time noise is about 0.5%.

Misses: time savings from truncation were larger than modelled (E028, E031). Time-neutral accuracy gains were over-predicted. Accuracy dropped on changes that cut signal.

Unsure: PCIe transfer of the bandwidth-bound levers (never measured here). Whether any further trim clears 0.753 on seeds 0-2. The tip is near the Pareto front, and further trims need an accuracy refund paid in epochs.

forecasts.reason: Diagnostic with no recipe change, so the numbers are the tip's. The profile likely shows non-GEMM kernels at 30% or more of the 32 px step.
Early low resolution is near free per E033, but this saves only about 0.08 s. The 3-seed accuracy sits within noise of the 0.753 gate, so the keep decision is a coin flip.
Removing 12 cheap 20 px steps saves about 2-3% of time. Accuracy is about -0.1 pp and the RNG re-roll adds noise, so it likely fails the 0.753 gate.
A staggered freeze lands between E036 and E037, with about half of E037's saving and half of its loss.
A 5 pp earlier freeze is a small dose, saving about 0.07 s at about -0.1 pp. It is within noise of the gate.
BN recalibration over 3 batches costs about 0.05 s. The gain is likely under 0.15 pp because the EMA already averages BN buffers.
16 px gives 1x1 final maps, a regime change like E018/E011 that probably costs 0.1-0.3 pp. The time saving is small.
Math-identical change, so accuracies stay bit-identical. It saves about 0.02-0.05 s of trial-0 overhead, averaged over 3 trials.

cruxes: Is the tip's population mean at or above 0.752, which decides whether any further time cut is feasible against the 0.75 bar?
Does an accuracy refund (epochs or batch size) cost less time than the remaining trims save?
Does the profile show the stem is still bandwidth-bound enough to matter, and will that transfer to the PCIe judge?
